definitions.explanation: Writing arranged in horizontal lines that run from left to right across the page. The standard writing direction for modern Japanese scientific, technical, and digital texts, as well as most web content.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{文書|ぶんしょ}→文書：12947_bunsho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{横書|よこが}きだ。
{横書|よこが}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{場合|ばあい}→場合：01704_baai⟧、⟦{数字|すうじ}→数字：03361_suuji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧アラビア⟦{数字|すうじ}→数字：03361_suuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: When writing horizontally, Arabic numerals are used.

examples.japanese: ⟦{教科書|きょうかしょ}→教科書：01085_kyoukasho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{理系|りけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{横書|よこが}き、{文系|ぶんけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{縦書|たてが}き→縦書き：13871_tategaki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧もの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Textbooks for science subjects are often written horizontally, while those for humanities are often vertical.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{横|よこ}→横：02984_yoko⟧ (horizontal, sideways) + {書|が}き (writing, from ⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧, to write). Literally "sideways writing."

USAGE:
Japanese can be written in two directions: {横書|よこが}き (horizontal, left to right) and ⟦{縦書|たてが}き→縦書き：13871_tategaki⟧ (vertical, top to bottom, columns right to left). Horizontal writing is standard for scientific texts, emails, web pages, and business documents. Vertical writing is traditional and still used for novels, newspapers, and formal documents. Many Japanese people switch between the two depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {横書|よこが}き⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to write horizontally
- {横書|よこが}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{文章|ぶんしょう}→文章：02957_bunshou⟧: horizontally written text
- {横書|よこが}き⟦{用|よう}→〜用：09842_you⟧: for horizontal writing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{縦書|たてが}き→縦書き：13871_tategaki⟧: vertical writing (the traditional counterpart)
